title: Why 3 days at work is the big AI promise that Bezos, Dimon, and Gates can't stop talking about
key_facts: Jeff Bezos, Amazon founder and chairman, told Fox News last week AI will let people do in three days what took five.
Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan Chase chief executive, has predicted the next generation will work three and a half days a week.
Eric Yuan, Zoom chief executive, said every company will support three or four days a week.
Bill Gates has said some people might work two or three days a week.
Sam Altman, OpenAI chief executive, said the promise of a four-hour week never arrives at mass scale.
Economist Alex Tabarrok said a shorter week is more likely than mass unemployment; the difference is distribution.
quote_evidence: "Some people will decide: 'I can support my family working three days a week,'" Amazon's founder and chairman said.
The "difference between catastrophe and wonderland boils down to distribution," Tabarrok wrote.
why_it_matters_hint: A set of top executives share a hopeful picture of AI and work that critics treat with caution.
notes: A roundup of statements made over months; Bezos's remark was 'last week'. Kept at 5 because the compilation and Tabarrok's comment are from this week.
